title: micro-surge-launch-navigator-and-release-notes-draft-2026-02
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a compact operational brief for the Micro-Surge launch window (short burst traffic + feature flag flip) for the runtime batching optimization change. Intended audience: release conductor, on-call SRE, serving-runtime owners, product PM.

High-level objectives:
- Validate that continuous-batching kernel selection reduces p50 token latency by ~8–12% for 32–64 sequence loads.
- Keep error-rate <= 0.5% above baseline during 90-minute surge window.
- Verify autoscale handoff within the Dedicated pool if load exceeds predicted runway.

Quick decision rules (read this first on launch day):
- Canary window (0–15m): if p50 increases > 15% OR 5xx rate > 0.5% above baseline -> abort and roll back to canary baseline (tag: canary-2026-02-12).
- Surge ramp (15–45m): if health signals stable and throughput improving, proceed to staggered 25% increments.
- Full flip (45–90m): require two consecutive 5-minute windows of p50 improvement and no error spike.

Checklist (pre-launch, D-2 to D-0):
- [ ] Confirm canary image built and signed: serving-runtime:v2026-02-12-aisha. Link: PR #987.
- [ ] Smoke tests green on staging with batching sim dataset (seq-dist A/B).
- [ ] Canary manifests uploaded to artifact registry and pinned in rollout manifest.
- [ ] Alert burn-in thresholds configured in prod: latency_alert (p50 + 15%), errors_alert (5xx delta 0.5%).
- [ ] Slack channel #launch-micro-surge created and people invited (see collaborators).
- [ ] Pager rotation aligned, escalation contacts confirmed: oncall-sre, svc-owner, patch-crew.
- [ ] Pre-generated rollback playbook checked into release binder (link to confluence page).
- [ ] Feature flag toggles and AB groups defined: ff-batching-optim (control|variant).
- [ ] Runbook quick checks printed as a single-page PDF for shift lead.

Deployment timeline (compact calendar):
- T-30m: launch channel open, checklist readout, config snapshots taken (k8s + autoscaler).
- T-20m: start canary deployment to 2% of traffic (or 1 node private pool).
- T-15m: monitor 5m window; decision: continue/rollback.
- T-10m: if green, move to 10% traffic.
- T+0–30m: step to 25% then 50% per 10–12m checks (staggered).
- T+30–90m: observe warm-up, watch for tail latency shifts; if steady, negotiate full flip.
- T+90m: post-mortem notes stubbed; begin extended sampling for 24h.

Observability and signals (who watches what):
- SRE dashboard: p50/p95/p99 token latency, 5xx rate, client timeout count, queue depth.
- Serving runtime: KV cache hit-rate, batch size distribution, GPU utilization per shard.
- Autoscaler: pod scale-up events, OOM/sigkill counts.
- Canary diff view: side-by-side of control vs variant metrics (link to dashboard RW-Canary-1).

Rollback triggers (explicit):
- Any sustained (>10m) p50 latency regression > 20% from baseline.
- Error budget burn > 1% in any 5-minute bucket.
- Repeated OOMs or node-level panics.
- Observed data corruption (rare but critical).

Rollback quick steps:
1) Flip ff-batching-optim -> control (immediate).
2) Scale down variant pods gracefully (drain) and scale control back up.
3) Run smoke test on degraded path and sanity checks.
4) Record timeline in #launch-micro-surge and open RW rollback ticket.

Communication plan (short):
- T-30m: Broad heads-up in #infra to announce window.
- Abort: post urgency note to #all-prod and mention affected customers (if any).
- Successful flip: note with short stats (p50, p95 delta, errors) and link to release notes.

Release notes (draft):
Title: runtime: continuous-batching kernel selection (micro-surge rollout)
Summary: Introduces adaptive kernel selection that picks optimized attention/dispatch kernels based on observed sequence-length distribution and workload batchability. Expected outcome: lower median token latency and improved throughput for mixed sequence workloads.
Changes included:
- Serving runtime: kernel selector v2 with sampling-based heuristics (PR #987).
- Runtime config: new batching.policy.alpha flag exposed to API and console.
- Observability: added batch-size histogram and KV-cache-hit gauge.

User-facing impact:
- Typical applications should see p50 token latency drop by ~10% in mixed workloads.
- No API surface change. Model outputs unchanged.

Known issues / caveats:
- In some very-low-batch micro-bursts, p99 latency may increase slightly due to scheduling heuristics — mitigation: fallback to legacy kernel on sustained tail regression.
- Internal metric names are experimental and will be renamed after 2 weeks of sampling.

Post-launch follow-up (owners & action items):
- Aisha: run 24h telemetry sampling and produce comparison report (RW-4603). Deadline: +48h.
- Mei: validate billing/usage telemetry for Dedicated pool impact (+72h).
- Tomás: run extended chaos simulation for node loss during batching (next sprint).
- Release-engineering: convert this doc into final release notes and archive runbook.

Notes to self / open questions:
- Do we need a short perf-sla for Dedicated customers during canary? (open: talk to contracts).
- Confirm whether function-calling customers are included in rollout test vector (cc: product).
- Should we add a short synthetic that triggers tiny-batch path to exercise fallback? (action: Mei to craft).

Appendix (quick snippets):
- Smoke test command: ./scripts/smoke-batch-test --seq-profile=mix32-64 --duration=300 --compare=baseline.json
- Canary manifest tag: manifests/canary/v2026-02-12-batching.yaml
- Dashboards: RW-Canary-1 | RW-Aggregate-latency | RW-Autoscale-events

End of brief. Keep this living — update notes inline with timestamps during run.
